newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU, Australia, ending rights row, sign pact.
newsitem.headline: EU, Australia, ending rights row, sign pact.

text.p: Australia and the European Union, ending months of acrimony over a human-rights clause, signed a pact on Thursday pledging closer cooperation in areas from trade to cultural ties.

In a statement, the European Commission said the pact would help promote a broader understanding between the two sides, strengthen cooperation on environmental protection and the fight against poverty, and set up closer contact in foreign affairs.
The pact, however, came in the form of a joint declaration rather than a legally binding agreement which is the EU norm in such circumstances.
Australia had refused throughout two years of negotiations to sign an agreement that contained a clause demanding that it respect human rights.
Such clauses are placed in all EU agreements as a matter of course and the 15-nation bloc refused to waive it for Australia fearing the precedent the move would create.
But at a signing ceremony on the margins of a sparsely attended EU foreign ministers meeting, both sides underlined their commitment to adhere to the declaration as if it were a full agreement.

"There is absolutely no difference in the level of commitment," European Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan said, underlining the EU's importance to Australia as its largest overseas economic partner.

Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer, who described the negotiations as "robust", said the declaration reflected to two sides' shared values including the protection and promotion of human rights.
